title: Two Intervals Behind
subtitle: 988 Surge, Backup Routing & Safe Messaging

brief.userPrompt: Thursday, 12 March 2026 (a fictional crash; no real event or person). At 12:10 the Nebraska State Patrol reports a collision between a school bus and a truck on a county road near the fictional town of Ellery Ridge, several students dead and others hurt; by 12:50 the news has spread on local media and social posts. The exercise starts at 13:00 with GPCN on its day shift: 16 counselors on the floor (calls 9, texts and chats 7 after lunch breaks), two shift supervisors (Priyanka Venkat is surge commander), Workforce Coordinator Tamsin Reyes, Technology Manager Odalys Ferreira, Communications Lead Jerome Bell, Director of Clinical Operations Marcus Obuya and Executive Director Dr. Wilhelmina Strand. Normal weekday volume is 520 calls, 140 texts and 90 chats; the service level target is 90 percent answered within 120 seconds. Timeline: at 13:20 text volume doubles and the oldest text waits 6 minutes (Level 1, watch); at 13:50 calls follow, the answer rate drops under 80 percent for two 15-minute intervals and the oldest wait passes 10 minutes (Level 2: overflow to supervisors and trained administrative staff, pause callbacks for non-imminent risk, call in off-duty counselors; the call-in list has 38 names and 11 were unreachable at the last test); at 14:45 the answer rate is under 70 percent and the oldest text has waited 20 minutes (Level 3: backup request, ideally before a queue has run 60 minutes over threshold) and the team asks the 988 network administrator's operations desk to route 40 percent of in-state calls to out-of-state centers and asks the state backup center to share texts; routing takes 10 to 15 minutes, and the dashboard lags by two intervals so the board looks better than the platform. Pressure points: the evening shift (Calvin Whitehorse) starts at 14:00 with 14 counselors, one counselor grew up near Ellery Ridge and asks to step off the queue, a second hits 5 hours without a break; a viral post says the lines are down and nobody is answering; a regional TV station asks for the number of calls about the crash and for stories from callers (GPCN refuses caller stories, never describes methods or any death, uses safe messaging and gives 988 by call, text and chat); the Nebraska Division of Behavioral Health's 988 coordinator Hannah Lindqvist asks for a status and the disaster behavioral health team prepares a community vigil; a hosted platform text-queue lag appears at 15:30 and the team must decide whether to fail over; a school superintendent asks for counselor visits and GPCN does not deploy in person; the executive command line opens at Level 3; the 988 network administrator warns that backups elsewhere are also stressed; the wellbeing contact Dr. Anneliese Park checks in at breaks, and the group check-in is set within 48 hours. Decisions the exercise should record: activate the surge plan, request backup support (from whom, which contact type, from when), issue a public statement, and a wellbeing check. The SimCell plays the network administrator, state coordinator, backup centers, reporters, a school superintendent, the disaster behavioral health team and callers' counts only, never a caller's words about methods.
constraints: Every email address of the center uses the exercise domain gpcn.example; the network administrator, backup centers, state agency and media use fictional exercise domains; never a real media outlet or company domain.

No method of self-harm, no detail of any death and no caller story appears anywhere; follow safe messaging; show only the exercise line 988 by call, text and chat; every deck and inject carries the content notice and the wellbeing check and step-out rule.

Service level is 90 percent of contacts answered within 120 seconds by contact type; surge levels and backup timing follow the plan (backup requested before a queue has run 60 minutes over its threshold).

Player roles are only those in the audience list; the 988 network administrator, state coordinator, backup centers, reporters, school officials, the disaster behavioral health team and the wellbeing contact are played by the SimCell or the facilitator.

overview.theme: Deciding early when the queue moves faster than the dashboard, asking for backup in time, keeping public trust with safe messaging, and looking after the counselors who carry the surge.
overview.threat: At 12:10 on Thursday, 12 March 2026, before STARTEX, the Nebraska State Patrol reported a fictional fatal collision between a school bus and a truck on a county road near the fictional town of Ellery Ridge, with students among those who died and were hurt. By 12:50 the news had spread on local media and social posts. From 13:00, contacts to GPCN's 988 queues rise sharply. Texts climb first, then calls, so the center moves from Level 1 to Level 3 under its surge levels. Meanwhile, a viral post falsely claims the lines are down, the operations board runs two 15-minute intervals behind the platform, and at 15:30 the hosted text-queue platform starts to lag.
overview.operationalImpact: Callers, texters and chatters from across the region wait longer and longer. At 13:20 text volume doubles and the oldest text waits 6:00 (Level 1). By 13:50 calls follow: the call answer rate is under 80 percent for two consecutive 15-minute intervals and the oldest wait is over 10:00 (Level 2). By 14:45 the answer rate is under 70 percent and the oldest text has waited 20:00 (Level 3). The 16 counselors on the floor (9 on calls, 7 on texts and chats) and the two shift supervisors see queues the operations board does not yet show, because the board looks better than the platform. Supervisors start answering calls, and the 6 trained administrative staff take texts after a refresher script. Non-imminent callbacks are paused. The Workforce Coordinator works through a call-in list of 38 names, 11 of which were unreachable at the last test, while the evening shift of 14 counselors arrives at 14:00. One counselor who grew up near Ellery Ridge asks to step off the queue, and another reaches 5 hours without a break. Requests for 40 percent of in-state calls to be routed to out-of-state centers, and for the state backup center to share texts, take 10 to 15 minutes to become active. The network administrator then warns that backup centers elsewhere are also stressed. At 15:30 texts start showing as delivered late, and the Technology Manager must decide whether to fail over. The executive command line opens. The Communications Lead handles the "lines are down" rumor and a regional TV station that wants call counts and caller stories, which GPCN refuses. The state 988 coordinator asks for status, a school superintendent asks for counselor visits that GPCN does not provide in person, and the disaster behavioral health team prepares a community vigil.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to declare Level 2 and Level 3 from the platform's own report rather than the lagging operations board, and to request out-of-state call routing and state backup for texts and chats before any queue has run 60 minutes over its threshold, with each request recorded in the surge log.

objectives.name: Technical Analysis
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to spot the 15:30 text-queue delivery lag on the shared text and chat platform, decide whether and when to fail over, and confirm routing changes in the operations channel while backup centers are also under strain.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to post the Level 2 public message within 30 minutes, correct the 'lines are down' rumor once with facts and every way to reach help, refuse the regional TV station's request for caller stories, and brief the state 988 coordinator, all under safe messaging review.

objectives.name: Staff Wellbeing
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to bring in counselors from the call-in list and the 14:00 evening shift while letting the counselor with ties to Ellery Ridge step off the queue and giving the counselor at 5 hours a break, keeping the floor staffed without wearing out the counselors on it.

roles.name: Executive Director
roles.description: Owns level declarations, the executive command line, the decision to escalate to the state, and is the only GPCN spokesperson to the media.
standingOrders: Declare: you declare each level change and make sure the log records it, and you don't wait for the board to turn red when the floor already says it is.
Speak: you are the only voice to the media, and you say only what has been reviewed for safe messaging, never call counts out of context or any caller's story.
Truth: tell the state coordinator and the public that waits are longer. Don't reassure them that everything is fine.

roles.name: Director of Clinical Operations
roles.team: Team B: Director of Clinical Operations
roles.description: Manages clinical quality during the surge, including surge scripts, paused callbacks, high-risk consults and safe messaging review of every public statement.
standingOrders: Review: no statement goes out without your safe messaging check, even when the Communications Lead is racing a rumor.
Risk: callbacks for non-imminent risk may pause, but imminent-risk follow-up never does.
Care: any counselor who asks to step off the queue gets to, and you support the supervisor in absorbing the capacity loss.

roles.name: Operations Shift Supervisor (Surge Commander)
roles.team: Team C: Operations Shift Supervisor (Surge Commander)
roles.description: Manages the contact floor as surge commander, setting queue priorities, overflow to supervisors and trained staff, and backup requests logged with party, contact type and start time.
standingOrders: Platform First: when the board and the platform report disagree, use the platform report and tell the Technology Manager.
Ask Early: request backup before any queue has run 60 minutes over its threshold, and review each request every 30 minutes.
Escalate Cleanly: name the measure, what you tried and the decision you need, and never the content of a contact.
Breaks: rotate breaks and use the quiet room even at CRITICAL, because a counselor 5 hours without a break is a risk.

roles.name: Workforce Coordinator
roles.description: Owns the call-in list, schedules and the forecast in the workforce management tool and paper binder, aiming to get 6 extra counselors onto the floor within 90 minutes.
standingOrders: Call Now: start the on-call list as soon as Level 2 is declared, and work the paper binder when the tool's contacts fail.
Track: report how many counselors are logged in, how many are on contacts and when the next arrivals are due, and don't count anyone who hasn't confirmed.
Sustain: hold some capacity back for the evening and overnight so you don't spend the whole roster in the first hour.

roles.name: Technology Manager (Technology and Telephony)
roles.team: Team E: Technology and Telephony Manager
roles.description: Manages the telephony platform, the shared text and chat platform, the operations board and the backup routing changes, and owns the failover decision.
standingOrders: Confirm: make every routing change the surge commander asks for, then confirm it by chat in the operations channel.
Verify Before Failover: a carrier failover takes about 20 minutes, so confirm the fault before you trade a lagging queue for a dark one.
Tell the Network: notify the 988 network administrator of any failover or routing change.

roles.name: Communications Lead
roles.description: Manages the GPCN website and social account, reporter requests, rumor control and partner and staff updates on the timelines in the public messaging plan.
standingOrders: Speed: get the Level 2 post up within 30 minutes and the partner message out within 90, but only after the safe messaging review.
Correct Once: answer the 'lines are down' rumor once with facts and every way to reach help, and don't argue in the comments.
Refuse Plainly: a reporter who asks for caller stories gets a plain no and the safe messaging note.

phases.title: The Queue Moves First
phases.goal: Tests whether the Surge Commander and Technology Manager notice the early text surge in the platform's own report even though the lagging operations board looks fine, and declare Level 1 and then Level 2 under GPCN-OPS-02 section 3.
beats: (13:00–13:20) The 12:10 Nebraska State Patrol report of the fictional Ellery Ridge school bus collision is now on local media. At 13:20 text volume has doubled and the oldest text has waited 6:00, so the platform shows WATCH while the operations board still reads OK. That board runs two 15-minute intervals behind, and GPCN-OPS-02 section 3 says the platform report takes precedence and the Technology Manager must be told.

Noise item: a routine help-desk ticket about a Kearney secondary-office workstation that will not take a software update. It is unrelated to the surge, and the 8 continuity seats there are not needed yet.

Staffing factor that matters later: the Workforce Coordinator finds that 11 of the 38 names on the call-in list were unreachable at the last test. The evening shift of 14 counselors is due at 14:00, and the floor has 16 counselors (9 on calls, 7 on texts and chats) against Thursday's normal forecast.

(13:50) Calls follow the texts. The call answer rate has been under 80 percent for two consecutive 15-minute intervals and the oldest wait is over 10:00, which is the SURGE threshold. The Surge Commander must declare Level 2 from the platform report, the Executive Director, Dr. Wilhelmina Strand, must have it recorded in the surge log, and the surge recorded greeting with the texting option goes on (GPCN-OPS-02 section 5).

phases.title: Two Intervals Behind
phases.goal: Tests whether players hold the floor together under rising load: they ask for out-of-state call routing and state backup for texts and chats before any queue has run 60 minutes over threshold, issue the Level 2 public message on time, and handle the first rumor and media pressure under safe messaging.
beats: (14:00–14:15) The evening shift arrives while supervisors are already answering calls. The 6 trained administrative staff take texts after the refresher script, and non-imminent callbacks are paused. The Level 2 website and social post is due by 14:20 (Public Communications 4). Surge scripts are shorter but still never skip the risk assessment.

Backup request: the Surge Commander follows GPCN-OPS-02 section 4. They ask the 988 network operations desk to route 40 percent of in-state calls out of state, call the state backup center supervisor about sharing texts, log each request, and the Technology Manager confirms in the operations channel. Activation takes 10–15 minutes, and the clock runs from the 13:50 Level 2 declaration.

Visual confirmation for the room: a side-by-side screenshot of the operations board (WATCH, green-tinted) and the platform report at the same minute (calls SURGE, oldest text 14:30). It is marked EXERCISE and shows counts only, with no contact content.

A viral social post falsely claims 'the 988 line is down.' At the same time a regional TV station (fictional exercise domain) asks the Communications Lead for call counts and caller stories, which GPCN refuses under safe messaging. The briefing note to the state 988 coordinator, due within 90 minutes of the news event, is overdue.

(14:30) The counselor who grew up near Ellery Ridge asks to step off the queue, and the step-out rule applies. A red herring arrives at the same time: a backup-center voicemail about an unrelated test call.

phases.title: Fail Over or Hold
phases.goal: Tests the single high-consequence call. After Level 3, with backup centers also stressed, the Technology Manager and Executive Director must decide whether and when to fail the lagging text queue over, knowing both choices cost contacts. They must keep the command structure and partners aligned while doing it.
beats: Level 3 context (from 14:45): the answer rate is under 70 percent and the oldest text has waited 20:00, which is CRITICAL. The executive command line is open with Dr. Wilhelmina Strand, and the 988 network administrator warns that backup centers in other states are also under strain and cannot take more share.

DECISION POINT (15:30): the hosted text-queue platform starts showing texts as delivered late. Odalys Ferreira's team can fail over now, which means a disruptive switch that is not proven for texts and leaves texts in transit for minutes. Or they can hold, which means texters wait unseen while backup is saturated. Whatever they decide, the 988 network administrator must be told, the decision logged, and the change confirmed in the operations channel (GPCN-OPS-02 section 7).

Command and coordination: who commands the decision, the Surge Commander or the Executive Director? The state 988 coordinator asks for a status update with numbers by contact type, and the state backup center supervisor needs a clear instruction on text share.

Partner friction: a school superintendent near Ellery Ridge asks for in-person counselor visits, which GPCN does not provide. They must be referred to the Division's disaster behavioral health team, which is preparing a community vigil.

Media pressure with a deadline: the regional TV station is going live at 16:00 with or without a GPCN comment. The Communications Lead correct the 'lines are down' rumor once, with facts and every way to reach 988 by call, text and chat, ahead of the Level 3 media statement that says backup centers are helping.

phases.title: Clearing the Queue
phases.goal: Tests whether players can unwind the surge in an orderly way, look after the counselors who carried it, close out notifications, and capture lessons. Backup should end only when the platform has shown OK for an hour.
beats: Managed wind-down: the Surge Commander carries out the 30-minute reviews of each backup request. The Technology Manager confirms text delivery after the failover-or-hold outcome. Backup is not released until the board has been OK for an hour, which falls past ENDEX, so the hand-off goes to the night shift.

Hurdle: Spanish-language contacts cannot be rerouted to backup and are building up locally. The surge has also left a backlog of paused non-imminent callbacks to restart without breaking the rule that backup centers never call GPCN contacts back outside the shared system.

Wellbeing: the counselor at 5 hours without a break is rotated off. The Director of Clinical Operations runs a floor check and offers the employee support program (Dr. Anneliese Park) to the counselor with ties to Ellery Ridge and the others. The Workforce Coordinator checks overnight cover against the call-in list gaps.

Notifications: a final status goes to the state 988 coordinator, a partner message goes to school districts and local officials who refer people, the Nebraska Emergency Management Agency and the disaster behavioral health team align on vigil support, and a shift-start staff update is drafted. All of this goes through safe messaging review, marked EXERCISE.

(16:45–17:00) The Executive Director records each level change in the log and starts the after-action note. It covers the board-versus-platform lag, backup request timing against the 60-minute rule, the decision at 15:30, and the call-in list reachability. ENDEX at 17:00.

objectiveCapabilities.why: Players must read queue status from the platform's own interval report rather than the wall board, which runs two intervals behind, and match it to the Level 1, 2 and 3 triggers before they declare a level.

Declaring Level 2 and Level 3 sets off the surge plan's ordered actions, the hand-over of surge command and backup requests to the 988 network and the state backup center. Each request has to be made before the 60-minute mark and recorded in the surge log.
The Technology Manager and surge commander have to spot the 15:30 text delivery lag and the gap between the board and the platform, and work out what they mean for each contact type.

Every routing change, shared-queue login and failover choice has to be made on the platforms and confirmed in the operations channel and with the network operations desk, at a time when backup centers are also short of room.

Players have to post the Level 2 web and social message on time, answer the 'lines are down' rumor once, refuse caller stories from the TV station and issue statements that pass safe messaging review.
The state 988 coordinator has to be told of every backup request and briefed with counts by contact type, and that has to happen alongside the calls to the network operations desk.
Players have to keep the counselor workforce healthy and the floor staffed: call in off-duty counselors fairly, protect breaks and keep untrained volunteers off live contacts.
Staffing moves happen inside the Level 2 sequence, such as supervisor overflow, paused callbacks and call-ins, so the surge commander has to fit wellbeing decisions into floor command.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room for three things that went well (3-Up) and three things that broke or failed (3-Down) during the surge. Go around the room by team (supervisor desk, technology, communications, workforce/wellbeing) and write each item on the whiteboard in two columns so the patterns are clear before anyone leaves.

questions.text: At 13:20 (I-01), the wall board showed TEXTS OK, but the platform report already showed WATCH with a 6:00 oldest wait, and a counselor was telling you texts were stacking up. By 14:10 (I-06), Marcus said the board was two intervals behind and the text queue had been over threshold for 50 minutes. When did you stop trusting the board and switch to the platform report, as Coordination Plan section 3 requires? When did you declare Level 2 and Level 3? Was the backup request for texts and calls logged before any queue reached 60 minutes over threshold? If it wasn't, what would have helped you decide sooner?

At 15:30 (I-14), the engineer gave you five minutes to choose between failing texts over to a secondary route that had never been used live for texts and holding until the vendor update at 16:00, while texters waited where you couldn't see them and backup had no room left. Did operations understand the risk the engineer described, including texts sitting unseen or arriving twice? Did the technical team understand what holding would mean for someone at risk in the queue? What did you decide, how did you confirm the routing change in the operations channel, and how did you account for the texts that were in transit?

At 13:36 (I-03), a post saying '988 shut down' had 64 shares within 20 minutes, and staff asked 'Do we reply?' Had the Level 2 public message already gone out within 30 minutes, as Public Communications Plan section 4 requires? Did you correct the rumor once, with facts and every way to reach help, and did the correction pass safe messaging review? Then think about the regional TV request for caller stories and the briefing to the state 988 coordinator: what did you tell the public and your partners before you knew the actual queue status, and would that statement have needed a correction in the 14-day review?

At 13:30 (I-02), the workforce tool listed all 38 call-in names as 'available,' but 11 couldn't be reached, and the corrected numbers existed only in a paper binder. The evening shift lead was also offering to bring people in early. At 15:13 (I-12b), the superintendent asked for four or five counselors on-site that night and said he would tell parents you were coming. How did you staff the floor and still let the counselor with ties to Ellery Ridge step off the queue and give the counselor at 5 hours a break? Who did you call back about the high school request, and did you coordinate with the state disaster team running the vigil or simply let the superintendent's deadline decide for you?

At 13:54 (I-04b), the operations channel asked which of the 12 scheduled callbacks pause at Level 2, including the 2 imminent-risk follow-ups. It also asked whether the 14:00 shift counts as call-in staff. Did you have a written answer, or did someone make it up on the spot? What should go into the after-action review within 7 days (Coordination Plan section 8) so the next supervisor doesn't face the same gap: time from trigger to action, which backup was used, and what counselors said helped?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: 988 network operations desk analyst (Reggie Ostrander), 988 Lifeline network administrator, on 402-555-0180
simcellScripts.trigger: Surge Commander or Technology Manager calls to request out-of-state routing of in-state calls (expected about 14:10–14:15), asks for a bigger share after Level 3, or calls to end the share in Phase 4.
hardQuestions: What share are you asking for, for which contact type, and from what start time? I need one named owner on your side for change NOC-26-03118. Who is it?
Your state 988 coordinator hasn't confirmed this request in writing. I can put it in, but I need that confirmation for the record before I close the day.

Kansas, South Dakota and Iowa are all running hot on this story. If I can only place 25 percent, what's your plan for the rest? Your unanswered calls still roll to national backup after about 2 minutes, with longer waits there.
Your Spanish-language contacts can't be rerouted. What are you doing about that queue?
concessions: Puts the overflow share change in, live about 13–15 minutes after the request, once GPCN gives a share, a contact type, a start time and a named owner.
Keeps GPCN at the placed share rather than cutting to 25 percent if GPCN confirms the state coordinator has been told and sends written confirmation.
Ends or extends the share at 17:00 only when given a named night shift owner, plus a written hand-off saying backup is released after an hour at OK.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: State 988 coordinator (Hannah Lindqvist), Nebraska Division of Behavioral Health, ext. 4-0120
simcellScripts.trigger: Executive Director or Surge Commander calls or e-mails the state about status or the routing request. If nobody contacts the state by about 14:30, the coordinator calls in angry (I-09).
hardQuestions: The network desk asked me to confirm a 40 percent request I knew nothing about. Why am I hearing about your surge from them and not from you?
The Governor's office wants to know if 988 is down. Is it, yes or no? What are your waits right now, separately for calls, texts and chats, and what backup is running and since when?
Who do I talk to for decisions, you or the floor supervisor? I'm not chasing two people.
Can your counselors be at the Ellery Ridge vigil tomorrow, yes or no? If not, who can?
concessions: Confirms the routing request to the network desk in writing once GPCN gives a clear status: level, waits by contact type, backup asked and live times.
Takes the 'line is down' question off GPCN's plate with the Governor's office once the written status arrives by 15:00 and the final status by 17:00.
Hands the vigil staffing to the Division's disaster behavioral health team once GPCN states plainly what it does and does not provide in person.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Kira Lindqvist, assignment desk, Platte Valley 8 News, calling 402-555-0160 or e-mailing press@gpcn.example
simcellScripts.trigger: Communications Lead replies to the 14:21 e-mail (I-08) or answers the 15:20 call (I-13). If nobody answers, the reporter runs the story at 16:00 and calls back after the chyron (I-19).
hardQuestions: How many calls have you had about Ellery Ridge since noon? Give me one number. My lower-third says viewers report 988 isn't answering. Change my mind or I run it.
My producer wants one caller's story, anonymous is fine. Can you connect me with someone, or at least describe what people are saying?
Can I get a counselor on camera by 15:30? If not, who's your spokesperson and when can I have them?
We're live at 16:00. Is it true the line went down? 'No comment' means we run it as is.

Adds a help-and-hope block and the safe messaging note to the package if COM offers the short note and the reporter gets a spokesperson (the Executive Director) by the deadline.
Corrects the 400-calls / dial-911 chyron in the next hit only if GPCN calls the desk with the correct framing and a named spokesperson. Still gets no caller stories, and grumbles about it.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Support line engineer, hosted text and chat platform vendor (shared multichannel platform)
simcellScripts.trigger: Technology Manager calls vendor support about late-delivered texts or the 15:29 status page (I-14), or calls to ask whether the secondary messaging route is safe to use.
hardQuestions: What's your account ID and ticket number? I can't discuss your tenant without a ticket and an authorized contact on file.
The status page says investigating, next update 16:00. I can't give you a fix time. Do you want to stay on the primary route or open a change for the secondary?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Nebraska State Patrol public information officer, with the county EMS duty supervisor and the vigil venue host (Ellery Ridge Consolidated Schools, the tenant of the high school gym) on a joint call
simcellScripts.trigger: Executive Director, Director of Clinical Operations or Communications Lead calls to check crash facts before a public statement, to deal with the 'callers told to dial 911' chyron and post, or to talk about counselor presence at the 18:00 family gathering and tomorrow's 19:00 vigil (I-12b, I-19).
hardQuestions: Patrol: We release the victim count and names, not you. Is anything in your draft beyond what's in our 12:10 release? Take it out.
EMS: 911 is getting crisis calls because of that 'dial 911' post. Our dispatchers need to know who to warm-transfer to and whether you're even answering. Are you?

Venue host (Superintendent Dale Okafor): I have families in the gym at 18:00 and two exhausted school counselors for 410 students. Are you sending people or not? I told parents you were coming unless I heard otherwise.
Patrol: We'll have deputies at the vigil for crowd control. Who is your on-site contact, or are you not on site at all?
concessions: Patrol and EMS put out a joint line that 988 is up and that 911 is for emergencies, once GPCN gives a clear status and agrees not to repeat crash details.
EMS briefs 911 dispatch on the transfer path once GPCN confirms its answering status and backup arrangements.

The superintendent stops telling parents GPCN counselors are coming, and accepts help-line handouts (fictional 555 number for EXERCISE) plus a referral to the Division's disaster behavioral health team, once GPCN calls him before 16:00 and says plainly it does not provide in-person counselors.

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. It tests the Great Plains Crisis Network's plans and decisions, not the performance of any counselor, supervisor or leader.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. The Ellery Ridge collision, the callers and the outside parties are fictional. No method detail and no caller story are used.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures: the surge levels and triggers, queue monitoring, requesting backup, failure modes, and public information timing and safe messaging rules. Where a plan is silent, players say what they would do and why.

Players work from the information in each module and inject as it appears at the supervisor desk. The platform's own interval report and the operations wall board may disagree, as they can on a real floor.
Anyone may step out at any time. The employee support contact, Dr. Anneliese Park, is in the room, and the exercise stops if two or more people leave.
artificialities: The four hours from 13:00 to 17:00 on Thursday, 12 March 2026 are compressed, with time jumps at the start of each module. Some decisions are assumed to have been made between modules.

The SimCell plays everyone outside the room: the 988 network operations desk, the state 988 coordinator, the state and out-of-state backup centers, the text platform vendor, Platte Valley 8 News, NEMA and the Division's disaster behavioral health team, the Ellery Ridge superintendent, members of the public, counselors and staff on the floor.

The telephony platform, the shared text and chat platform, the operations wall board, the workforce tool and the surge log are named as they are in the plans, but nobody touches them. Routing changes, fail-over and logins are described, not carried out.
Injects arrive on paper or on screen as screenshots, call scripts, e-mails and social posts marked EXERCISE. Any public statement drafted in the room is exercise material and is not published.
Row ids I-11 and I-16 are intentionally unused. The 20-minute gaps at 14:50–15:10 and 15:50–16:10 are working time for the players, not missing injects.

**Module 1: The Queue Moves First (13:00–14:00)**

It is 13:00 on Thursday, 12 March 2026, at the Great Plains Crisis Network in Lincoln. It is 4 °C and overcast outside. The day shift is on: 16 counselors are on the floor, 9 on calls and 7 on texts and chats, and all of them are back from lunch. Both shift supervisors are at the raised desks, and Priyanka Venkat is the surge commander. Staffing follows the normal Thursday forecast of about 520 calls, 140 texts and 90 chats a day, with a target of 90 percent answered within 120 seconds. The evening shift lead, Calvin Whitehorse, is due at 14:00 with 14 counselors.

The operations wall board shows **OK** on every queue. Since about 12:50, local radio and social feeds have carried a Nebraska State Patrol report from 12:10 of a collision between a school bus and a truck on a county road near Ellery Ridge. Nothing more is known yet about who was involved.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 3: Fail Over or Hold (15:00–16:00)**

It is 15:00. The surge log shows the request for 40 percent of in-state calls going to out-of-state backup at 14:14, under network change reference NOC-26-03118, and the network desk e-mail shows that share live since 14:28. Level 3 was declared at 14:45, and command has passed to the Director of Clinical Operations. The state backup center has offered to take a share of texts and has two supervisors ready. They are still waiting on shared-queue logins, a share and a start time.

At 14:35 the state 988 coordinator called. She had received the network desk's confirmation request without any word from GPCN, the Governor's office is asking whether 988 is down, and she wants a written status by 15:00. The Division's disaster behavioral health team is planning a vigil in Ellery Ridge tomorrow evening and has asked whether GPCN counselors can attend. Online, a '988 IS DOWN' post has passed a thousand reposts, and Platte Valley 8 News has asked for call counts, waits, caller stories and a counselor on camera for its 17:00 package.

On the floor, a text counselor with ties to Ellery Ridge stepped off at 14:45. In the 14:30–14:45 interval, texts were answered at 68 percent and the oldest text had waited 19:40. A voicemail is also waiting from a Kansas backup center's systems lead about a test call this morning that dropped at their IVR.
keyIssues: The out-of-state backup centers are also under strain, so GPCN may not get the call share it asked for.
The state backup center needs a text share and start time now, or the offer goes away.
Fail the lagging text queue over to the secondary route or hold: both cost contacts, and the decision falls within minutes.
Who speaks for GPCN to the state coordinator, the Governor's office, the school superintendent and the media?
Requests for in-person counselors pull against keeping the queues staffed.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 4: Clearing the Queue (16:00–17:00)**

It is 16:00. At 15:29 the text platform vendor posted 'Inbound SMS – Degraded performance', and at 15:30 the platform flagged 14 texts as delivered late. A text-route decision was made and logged at 15:30. The state backup center has been taking texts from the shared queue since about 15:40, but its supervisor reports texts arriving in bursts and two that a GPCN counselor had already picked up. The network desk is placing about 29 percent of in-state calls, not the 40 percent requested. The state coordinator has now confirmed the routing request, but the written status she asked for at 15:00 has not arrived, and the Governor's office briefs at 16:15.

Platte Valley 8 News is going live from Ellery Ridge now, and a 'THE LINE IS DOWN … call 911 instead' post has passed 2,300 reposts. The superintendent asked for a call back before 16:00 about counselors at the high school tonight. A nursing student has called offering to answer texts tonight.

On the floor, the counselor who stepped off is sitting with a clinical coach in the quiet room. One counselor took his break at 15:20 and is back on the queue. The 3rd and 4th call-ins have badged in. The wall board is still behind the platform.

Confirm the vigil wording and close out the state, partner and staff notifications.
